ashe-in-america.title: Ashe in America
ashe-in-america.body:
Ashe in America is a writer and contributor to [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] who publishes commentary on the Badlands Brief, focusing heavily on election integrity and Democratic Party politics.[{n}]

## Commentary in the July 28, 2026 Brief

On the appeals court ruling against President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s election administration order, she wrote that "Saturday's decision does not settle the underlying dispute over presidential power but keeps [[indira-talwani|Talwani]]'s injunction intact while the case winds through the courts, a delay that could push final resolution dangerously close to the midterms."[{n}]

On [[axios|Axios]]'s 2028 Democratic power rankings, she responded "Yes, please," calling it "really quite something that there is no new talent on the Democrat side" and "hilarious that we're talking about [[alexandria-ocasio-cortez|AOC]] being anywhere near executive power."[{n}] She argued she would be concerned only if Democrats were elevating "someone new, someone that seems normal and Kennedy-esque" who tacked back to the middle and restored sanity, whereas [[kamala-harris|Harris]], [[gavin-newsom|Newsom]] and AOC are "punchlines" proving the party is not interested in competent contenders — because "all these people know elections are fake."[{n}] She closed by asking how far "this DSA Rising op" will go and when the [[bernie-sanders|Bernie Sanders]] comeback arrives.[{n}]

ghostofbasedpatrickhenry.title: GhostofBasedPatrickHenry
ghostofbasedpatrickhenry.body:
GhostofBasedPatrickHenry is a writer and Badlands Brief contributor whose commentary focuses on [[israel|Israel]], the Middle East, and the narcotics war in the Western Hemisphere.[{n}]

## Israel and Turkey

In the July 28, 2026 Brief he identified "another pattern emerging": the last time [[benjamin-netanyahu|Netanyahu]] "tried to crash the White House," in September 2025 during the UN General Assembly, [[donald-trump|Trump]] reacted by inviting [[recep-tayyip-erdogan|Erdogan]] to the White House the day before Netanyahu was to address the assembly — and with Netanyahu again inviting himself, Trump was again using Erdogan to signal his real intent.[{n}] He argued Trump's plan is not kinetic war against "America's greatest foreign adversary" but the destruction of Israel's public reputation by allowing it "the space to show the world what it truly is," with the war against Iran costing Israel fifteen years of accumulated goodwill.[{n}] He described Israel as an empire modeled on the ancient Sanhedrin, seeking "only the glory for itself," and said he would be watching Trump's engagement with Netanyahu, what he offers, what moves follow against [[turkey|Turkey]], and when Russia gets involved.[{n}]

## Cartels and Mexico

He recounted Colombian President [[gustavo-petro|Gustavo Petro]]'s February 2025 claim that Colombian jungle militias were proxies of the [[sinaloa-cartel|Sinaloa cartel]], noted the Trump administration's indictment of ten Mexican officials for cartel ties, and criticized [[claudia-sheinbaum|Claudia Sheinbaum]]'s reluctance to help fight the cocaine cartels.[{n}] He asked why the press seems more concerned with whether the US military will invade [[mexico|Mexico]] than with Americans dying on behalf of a foreign country, argued that the cartels, press and corrupt politicians are all part of "a larger cartel that seeks to rule the world," and held that the only war America should fight is "the war to secure our border, secure our elections, and save our country" — with fully understanding "the treason and fraud that has occurred in and around our government" among its most important objectives.[{n}]

burning-bright.title: Burning Bright
burning-bright.body:
Burning Bright is the pen name of a writer and contributor to [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] whose work applies fifth-generation warfare framing to political and technological developments.[{n}]

## The AI Shadow War

On the Devolution Power Hour in late July 2026, Burning Bright argued at length about "the topic that almost nobody in the [[truth-community|Truth Community]] is paying attention to right now," which he believes "has more to do with alternatively starting or stopping the American Golden Age than almost anything else we spend our time arguing about."[{n}] He claimed the concerted effort by [[sam-altman|Sam Altman]] of [[openai|OpenAI]] and [[dario-amodei|Dario Amodei]] of [[anthropic|Anthropic]] to seek government regulation was an attempt to slow and control the AI push, putting it "in collectivist, oligarchic hands," making the two men "retardants" rather than "accelerants" to the AI agenda.[{n}] That distinction, he argued, explains how audiences can be broadly correct in their anxieties about AI's "serpentine" core personalities while missing that [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] is pinning much of his futurism agenda on AI's acceleration.[{n}]

He cited three weekend developments as making his takes "age rapidly, and quite well": former White House AI and Crypto Czar [[david-sacks|David Sacks]] echoing his framing almost beat for beat; Commerce Secretary [[howard-lutnick|Howard Lutnick]] reportedly saying the administration aims to "protect open source AI"; and [[china|China]] timing strategic releases of open-weight models that accelerate the industry while blunting Western attempts to slow it, granting Trump narrative shielding.[{n}] His conclusion was that China is "actually HELPING protect the future of an open-source, open-weight, FREE AI world," and that it is a "good thing Trump and [[xi-jinping|Xi]] are Sovereign Bros."[{n}]

badlands-media.title: Badlands Media
badlands-media.body:
## The Badlands Brief

Badlands Media publishes the Badlands Brief, described as "your daily drop of Badlands' takes on the narratives dominating the info war," inviting readers to join the conversation in the comments section.[{n}] The July 28, 2026 edition, titled "Entertaining Obstruction & Artificial Shadow Wars," carried commentary from [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]], [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] and [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] on the Trump election order litigation, the [[open-source-artificial-intelligence|open-source AI]] fight, [[benjamin-netanyahu|Netanyahu]] and American opinion of [[israel|Israel]], the 2028 Democratic field, and the cartel campaign in [[mexico|Mexico]].[{n}] The Brief carries a standing disclaimer that opinions expressed are those of the tagged authors and do not necessarily reflect the attitudes or positions of Badlands Media, and directs readers to the outlet's shows streaming on Rumble; the Brief is free, supported by optional paid subscriptions.[{n}]

truth-community.title: Truth Community
truth-community.body:
## Blind spot on artificial intelligence

[[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] used the term "Truth Community" in July 2026 to describe the alternative-media audience he addresses, arguing that the fight over [[open-source-artificial-intelligence|open-source artificial intelligence]] is "the topic that almost nobody in the Truth Community is paying attention to right now," despite having more bearing on "alternatively starting or stopping the American Golden Age than almost anything else we spend our time arguing about."[{n}] He held that members of this audience can be broadly correct in their anxieties about the AI push, given how "serpentine" its core personalities are, while completely missing that [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] has staked much of his futurism agenda on AI's acceleration.[{n}]

white-house.title: White House
white-house.body:
## Cartel policy and AI (2026)

Amid reporting that the [[donald-trump|Trump]] administration was preparing options for military action inside [[mexico|Mexico]], the White House maintained that its focus is dismantling transnational criminal organizations responsible for fentanyl trafficking, human smuggling and violence affecting the United States, with officials emphasizing cooperation with Mexico where possible while declining to rule out additional measures against cartel leadership.[{n}]

On technology policy, White House Commerce Secretary [[howard-lutnick|Howard Lutnick]] reportedly said the administration aims to "protect open source AI," and former White House AI and Crypto Czar [[david-sacks|David Sacks]] argued that [[openai|OpenAI]] and [[anthropic|Anthropic]] seek regulation to stave off competitors.[{n}] [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] separately framed [[benjamin-netanyahu|Netanyahu]]'s repeated efforts to secure White House visits as a recurring pattern that Trump answers by elevating [[recep-tayyip-erdogan|Erdogan]].[{n}]
